record.paper_title: Exactly unsolved problems of interacting 1D fermions
record.context_brief: infrared divergences in massless form-factor perturbation theory
record.original_question: For massless boundary sine-Gordon form-factor expansions perturbed by terms such as cos φ or by the field φ itself, what partial resummation of the most infrared-divergent perturbative terms is needed to make the expansion usable for the quantum-dot, quantum-Hall-interferometer, and double-barrier transport problems?

evidence.quote: The basic unperturbed model is the massless sine-Gordon model with the interaction (cosine) term restricted to one point, which is integrable. It is being perturbed by the second interaction term, V (φ), which destroys the integrability.

In all the three problems one has to deal with IR divergences in the form-factor expansion, since the perturbing terms are either cos φ or field φ itself. Such divergences are peculiar for the masssless theories.
The partial resummation of the most divergent terms of the perturbation series is necessary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the massless sine-Gordon model on the half-line (boundary sine-Gordon model): a free massless bosonic field φ(x,t) on x ≥ 0 with a boundary cosine interaction g cos(βφ(0,t)) localized at x = 0. At the boundary, this integrable theory admits an exact massless S-matrix and an associated form-factor expansion for correlation functions of local operators.

Perturb this integrable model by an additional non-integrable interaction V(φ), of one of the following two physically relevant types:
  (a) V(φ) = λ cos(αφ(0,t)) with α ≠ β (a second cosine, as arises in models of a quantum dot and of double-barrier resonant tunneling in a Luttinger liquid),
  (b) V(φ) = h·φ(0,t) (a linear coupling to the boson, as arises in the quantum-Hall point-contact interferometer geometry).

Expand physical observables (e.g., conductance, tunneling current, noise) as a perturbation series in V using the form-factor representation of correlators of the unperturbed integrable boundary theory. Because the unperturbed theory is massless and the perturbing operators are either cos(αφ) or φ itself, each order of the perturbative series exhibits infrared divergences arising from the gapless spectrum.

Problem: Identify and carry out an explicit partial resummation of the most infrared-divergent contributions, to all orders in V, that produces an infrared-finite form-factor perturbative expansion suitable for computing transport quantities in the three physical settings above (quantum dot, quantum-Hall interferometer, and double-barrier transport). Equivalently, determine the leading IR-divergent class of diagrams in the form-factor expansion of the boundary sine-Gordon model perturbed by V(φ) and resum it into a closed expression that renders the remaining series IR-finite.
artifact.status_search_result: A search for IR-divergence resummation of form-factor perturbation series in the massless boundary sine-Gordon model with cos φ or linear φ perturbations did not return a specific construction addressing the quantum-dot, quantum-Hall-interferometer, and double-barrier transport problems simultaneously. General form-factor resummation techniques exist for massive and bulk massless sine-Gordon settings, but a definitive resolution of the required partial resummation in this boundary perturbed setting is not clearly documented; status is unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Form Factor Perturbation Theory (hep-th/9406125)
status_evidence.snippet: Form Factor Perturbation Theory is used to analyse the evolution of the spectrum of particle excitations when treating a theory as a perturbed Sine-Gordon model.
status_evidence.claim: Form-factor perturbation theory is a known framework for perturbed sine-Gordon, but IR-divergence resummation specific to massless boundary problems is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Non-integrable aspects of the multi-frequency Sine-Gordon model
status_evidence.snippet: Multi-frequency (two-cosine) sine-Gordon model studied via form-factor perturbation theory.
status_evidence.claim: Related double-cosine perturbations have been studied, but the specific boundary-massless IR resummation question is not explicitly settled.
